item.title: Business activity slumps across Europe, India and Asia amid Iran war
item.description: Business activity across the eurozone, India and parts of Asia slowed sharply in March as the war in the Middle East drove energy prices higher and sapped demand, according to flash purchasing managers' index data released Tuesday by S&P Global. The surveys, conducted between March 12 and March 20, offer the first broad snapshot of economic damage since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.

item.title: Foreign investors pull $50B from Asian stocks in record March exodus
item.description: Global financial markets remain gripped by volatility as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fourth week, with oil prices climbing back above $100 a barrel and foreign investors fleeing Asian equities at a pace not seen since the 2008 financial crisis. Data from LSEG shows approximately $50 billion in net foreign equity outflows from South Korea, Taiwan, India, and Southeast Asian markets throughout March, positioning 2026 for the largest monthly capital flight from the region in nearly two decades.

item.title: UN report finds freshwater fish migrations collapsing worldwide
item.description:
Some of the longest and most important animal migrations on Earth are happening beneath the surface of the world's rivers — and many are rapidly collapsing. That is the finding of a major new assessment released on Monday at the UN's Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species (CMS) conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, which identifies hundreds of freshwater fish species in urgent need of international protection.

The Global Assessment of Migratory Freshwater Fishes, described as the most comprehensive overview ever assembled of migratory freshwater fish conservation needs, found that populations of migratory freshwater fish have declined by roughly 81 percent since 1970. Nearly all — 97 percent — of the 58 CMS-listed migratory fish species are now threatened with extinction.

item.title: Study finds Europe's last Neanderthals descended from one small group
item.description: Europe's last Neanderthals descended from a single small population that survived harsh Ice Age conditions by retreating to a climate refuge in what is now southwestern France, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The finding adds to a growing body of genetic evidence showing that severe losses of diversity plagued Neanderthal populations long before their final disappearance roughly 40,000 years ago.

item.title: Astronomers crack two 50-year stellar mysteries in rapid succession
item.description: Two long-standing puzzles in stellar astrophysics have been cracked in rapid succession, with researchers announcing breakthroughs on both the enigmatic surface chemistry of red giant stars and the origin of unusual X-rays from one of the night sky's most visible stars.

item.title: Israel to occupy southern Lebanon up to Litani River, defence minister says
item.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared on Tuesday that the Israeli military will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River, marking the first time Israel has explicitly stated its intent to seize territory amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon.

item.title: Russia launches 16 Rassvet satellites to rival Starlink
item.description: Russian private aerospace company Bureau 1440 launched 16 low-Earth orbit satellites on Monday as part of its Rassvet constellation, a state-backed broadband internet project intended to serve as Moscow's answer to SpaceX's Starlink. The launch from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome marks Russia's first step toward building a domestic satellite internet network, though the effort remains dwarfed by its American competitor.

item.title: NASA cancels lunar orbit station, pivots to $20B moon base
item.description:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman on Tuesday announced the agency will cancel its planned Gateway space station in lunar orbit and instead redirect its components toward building a base on the moon's surface, a $20 billion effort expected to take seven years.

"It should not really surprise anyone that we are pausing Gateway in its current form and focusing on infrastructure that supports sustained operations on the lunar surface," Isaacman told attendees at a day-long event at NASA headquarters in Washington.

item.title: NASA visualization shows GUARDIAN spotted tsunami 32 minutes before tide gauges
item.description: NASA released a new data visualization this week showing how its experimental GUARDIAN tsunami detection system spotted an incoming wave near Hawaii a full 32 minutes before conventional tide gauges during last summer's massive Kamchatka earthquake, underscoring the technology's potential to give coastal communities precious extra time to evacuate.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, UAE edge toward joining war on Iran
item.description:
Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are edging toward direct involvement in the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, with Riyadh opening a key air base to American forces and Abu Dhabi dismantling Iranian institutional presence on its soil, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

The moves mark a turning point for two Gulf monarchies that initially lobbied Washington against military action on Iran but have been drawn deeper into the conflict by weeks of Iranian missile and drone strikes on their territory and energy infrastructure.

item.title: Iran fears ceasefire talks are a trap to kill its remaining leaders
item.description:
Iranian officials believe that U.S. efforts to broker a ceasefire may be a ploy to expose the country's surviving senior leadership to assassination, according to The Wall Street Journal. Tehran is particularly concerned that face-to-face negotiations could be used as a pretext to target Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament and a former paramilitary commander, whom Washington has sought to bring to the table.

Ghalibaf has so far managed to avoid the Israeli strikes that have killed a succession of top Iranian figures, making him one of the few high-ranking officials still alive. The fears were relayed by Iranian officials to Arab counterparts, the Journal reported Monday.

item.title: Stocks slide as Iran strikes dash hopes for quick end to war
item.description: Oil prices climbed and U.S. stocks slid on Tuesday as Iranian missile strikes across the Middle East undercut hopes for a swift end to the nearly four-week-old conflict between Iran and the U.S.-Israeli coalition. The renewed attacks came just a day after President Trump claimed progress in negotiations with Tehran — assertions Iran flatly denied.

item.title: Saudi crown prince urges Trump to escalate Iran war, deploy ground troops
item.description:
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has been pressing President Donald Trump in a series of private conversations to continue and even escalate the war against Iran, arguing that the U.S.-Israeli military campaign presents a "historic opportunity" to reshape the Middle East by toppling the government in Tehran, according to a New York Times report citing people briefed by U.S. officials on the conversations.

The revelation comes as the conflict enters its fourth week and Trump has sent mixed signals about its direction, at one point saying he was considering "winding down" military operations.

item.title: OpenAI Foundation pledges $1B in grants for AI safety and health research
item.description: The OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit arm that controls the artificial intelligence company behind ChatGPT, announced Tuesday that it plans to grant $1 billion over the next year to fund AI safety, health research, and efforts to mitigate the technology's societal risks. The pledge marks a dramatic escalation in the organization's philanthropic activity, coming just months after OpenAI restructured into a conventional for-profit business.

item.title: 20-year study finds mammal cloning hits genetic dead end after 58 generations
item.description:
A 20-year experiment in Japan has revealed that mammals cannot be cloned indefinitely, with researchers producing 58 generations of mice from a single donor before the cloned animals accumulated so many genetic mutations they could not survive past their first day of life.

The study, published Tuesday in Nature Communications, was led by geneticist Sayaka Wakayama and developmental biologist Teruhiko Wakayama at the University of Yamanashi. Beginning in 2005, the team used somatic cell nuclear transfer — the same technique that produced Dolly the sheep — to serially clone a single female mouse, producing more than 1,200 offspring across nearly six decades of clonal generations.

item.title: Altman exits Helion board as OpenAI eyes massive fusion deal
item.description:
OpenAI is negotiating a massive power purchase agreement with fusion startup Helion Energy that could deliver 5 gigawatts of electricity by 2030 and scale to 50 gigawatts by 2035, according to a report by Axios on Monday citing a person familiar with the talks. Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO and Helion's largest individual investor, has stepped down from Helion's board of directors to avoid conflicts of interest as the two companies move toward a partnership.

The proposed deal would give OpenAI a guaranteed 12.5% share of Helion's projected energy output, dwarfing every existing commercial fusion agreement. For context, Helion's only signed power contracts to date are a 50-megawatt deal with Microsoft struck in 2023 and a 500-megawatt plant being developed with steelmaker Nucor — making the OpenAI framework 100 to 1,000 times larger than anything the company has committed to before.

item.title: Modi warns of 'serious consequences' as Hormuz crisis deepens
item.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday, with both leaders stressing the need to keep the Strait of Hormuz open as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran continues to disrupt global energy supplies and rattle economies worldwide.

Trump initiated the call, according to U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, who said on X that the two leaders "discussed the ongoing situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open". Modi, in his own post on X, said he had a "useful exchange of views" and reiterated India's position. "India supports de-escalation and restoration of peace at the earliest. Ensuring that the Strait of Hormuz remains open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world," Modi wrote.

item.title: EU delays proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports
item.description:
The European Commission will no longer submit a legal proposal to permanently ban Russian oil imports on April 15 as previously planned, an updated EU legislative agenda showed on Tuesday, as the war in Iran sends global crude prices to their highest levels in years.

An EU official told Reuters the proposal had not been cancelled and would still be published, though no longer by the mid-April date due to "current geopolitical developments."

item.title: Oil tops $100 again as Iran strikes Israel, Gulf states
item.description: A fresh barrage of Iranian missiles targeting Israel and Gulf Arab states on Tuesday sent oil prices climbing again, boosting Canada's energy-heavy stock market while dragging Wall Street lower as investors grappled with the four-week-old conflict's toll on the global economy.

item.title: NASA highlights starshade concept for imaging Earth-like exoplanets
item.description: NASA is pushing forward on multiple fronts in its quest to directly photograph planets orbiting distant stars, with a wave of new missions, research breakthroughs, and industry partnerships coming together in early 2026 to lay the groundwork for finding another Earth.
